chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever has intercourse with his wife once, and then is seized (from it), there is no choice for her.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a wife's right to annul marriage if her husband is impotent after consummation?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the legal status of 'khiyar al-‘ayb' (option of defect) in cases of male impotence, establishing that a single consummation suffices to validate the marriage contract and preclude the wife's right to annulment. Scholars note this ruling emphasizes the finality of marital bonds once the essential act is performed, distinguishing it from cases where impotence is discovered before any intercourse occurs. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that consummation cures the defect for the purpose of marital stability.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who goes to his wife once, then he is seized from it, so there is no choice for her’.
en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
’Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘If a man only once goes to bed with his wife then is held back (by magic), no choice then remains for her (to revoke the marriage).”’
